identity.title: Food Safety Plan for Ready-to-eat Hummus and Bean Dips

scan.summary: This is a written Food Safety Plan required under FDA's Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Preventive Controls rule, covering the company's production of refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips. The plan identifies biological, chemical, and physical hazards in the manufacturing process and describes the preventive controls, monitoring procedures, and corrective actions the facility must follow. The company must keep records of all monitoring and corrective actions, maintain thermometer calibration and metal detector function, conduct monthly product testing for Listeria, and obtain certificates from approved suppliers.
scan.freshness_note: This plan is dated May 12, 2025, and is now 16 months old as of September 29, 2026. Under FSMA, food safety plans must be reanalyzed at least once every three years, so a reanalysis would not be due until May 2028. However, a plan this age in an operational facility should be regularly monitored and may need updating if operations or hazards change. Consider requesting the most recent corrective action logs and verification records to confirm the plan is still being followed.

gaps.title: Reanalysis schedule not stated
gaps.description: The plan does not state when it will be reanalyzed or when the next reanalysis is due. FDA requires reanalysis at least once every three years, and the plan should document the schedule.
gaps.fix: Add a section stating: 'This Food Safety Plan will be reanalyzed by [date three years from effective date], and thereafter at least once every three years, or sooner if operations change or a preventive control is found ineffective.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80(b) and FDA FSMA Preventive Controls rule

gaps.title: Validation of preventive controls not documented
gaps.description: The plan describes monitoring procedures but does not clearly state that the preventive controls have been validated—meaning tested to confirm they will actually achieve the critical limits and prevent hazards. The cook time/temperature control and cooling parameters should be validated with supporting documentation.
gaps.fix: Add a Validation section stating which controls have been validated, by whom, on what date, and referencing any supporting data (e.g., time-temperature studies, published guidelines, or expert reports).
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80(b) and FDA Guidance on Food Safety Plans
gaps.locator: Section 7 mentions verification and monthly testing but not initial validation of critical limits

gaps.title: Recall plan not included
gaps.description: FDA's Preventive Controls rule requires a written recall plan as part of the Food Safety Plan. This document does not include procedures for product recall, notification, or traceability in the event of a food safety incident or product defect.
gaps.fix: Add a new section (11. Recall Plan) that documents: product traceability and lot identification, procedures for identifying affected product, customer notification procedures, documentation retention, and roles and responsibilities for recall execution.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80(b)(5) — Preventive Controls for Human Food rule requires 'a recall plan'

gaps.title: Listeria spp. detection method and action level not specified
gaps.description: The plan states that environmental monitoring uses Listeria spp. swabs weekly and that finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly, but does not specify the detection method (culture, PCR, etc.), reporting threshold (CFU/swab or mL), or the action level that triggers corrective action beyond retesting.
gaps.fix: Add detail to Section 4 and 7: 'Environmental monitoring and finished product testing will use [method], with a reportable limit of [X CFU]. Positive results for Listeria spp. at [X CFU/swab or higher] will trigger corrective actions as described in Section 6.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80(b) and FDA guidance on Listeria monitoring in RTE foods
gaps.quote: Finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory

gaps.title: PCQI transition or absence plan not documented
gaps.description: The plan names Dana Whitfield as the PCQI, trained in March 2024. The plan does not state what will happen if this individual leaves, is unavailable, or if their FSPCA certificate expires. FDA requires that a PCQI oversee the plan.
gaps.fix: Add a statement: 'Should the PCQI become unavailable, [backup individual name or qualifications] will assume PCQI responsibilities pending recruitment or retraining. The PCQI's FSPCA certificate and qualifications will be reviewed annually.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.180(a) and FDA guidance on PCQI responsibilities
gaps.quote: Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)

gaps.title: Sanitation control critical limits not fully defined
gaps.description: The plan states that ATP swab results must show a 'pass' before start-up and that a washdown is 'verified by ATP swab before the next non-sesame product,' but does not define what constitutes a 'pass' (specific ATP value in RLU) or the exact surface area tested.
gaps.fix: Specify ATP swab acceptance criteria, e.g., 'ATP swabs must read ≤150 RLU for food-contact surfaces and ≤300 RLU for non-food-contact surfaces per [industry standard or company standard].'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80(b)(3) — sanitation controls must have defined critical limits or parameters
gaps.quote: ATP swab pass before start-up; Listeria spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2

gaps.title: Training records and competency verification not addressed
gaps.description: Section 10 states that production employees receive training 'at hire and annually' and that leads are 'trained on the monitoring procedures,' but the plan does not require documentation of training completion, competency assessment, or records retention.
gaps.fix: Add to Section 10: 'Training records documenting date, content, and employee signature will be maintained for all production employees. Competency will be verified annually by the PCQI or designee through review of performance or practical assessment.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80(b) (Food Safety Plan) and 21 CFR 117.180(e) (personnel training and supervision requirements)
gaps.quote: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually

facts.affects: Tahini (sesame paste) is a significant hazard requiring allergen labeling review and cross-contact prevention; bean dips (without tahini) do not carry this allergen

scan.confidence_notes: HIGH confidence in the overall accuracy of the gaps and facts identified. I have read the entire document carefully and matched it against FDA's Preventive Controls rule (21 CFR Part 117) and FSMA guidance. The document is well-structured, clearly written, and contains the core elements of a food safety plan (hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, and supply-chain program). MEDIUM confidence that I have identified all gaps: the major gaps (missing recall plan, lack of validation documentation, no reanalysis schedule) are clearly omitted from the text. However, some gaps (like the specific ATP swab threshold) may be documented in training materials, standard operating procedures, or logs not provided here. The document is a policy/plan document issued and approved by the company's Plant Manager, and the effective date of May 12, 2025, is stated. Oregon Department of Agriculture would be the state regulator, and FDA would be the federal regulator under FSMA. I note that the plan does not reference any FDA establishment number or submission of a qualified facility attestation, which the company should have on file separately. LOWER confidence on whether Oregon state law imposes additional requirements beyond FDA's federal rule; I have not located a state-specific food safety plan requirement beyond FDA's FSMA rule.

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.

Metal Metal detection of every sealed tub Process Reject at 2.0 mm ferrous, 2.5 mm non-
ferrous, 3.0 mm stainless test pieces
5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
